text: The night Mo hatched out of his egg, the whole valley heard the sound.
Not a bang.
Not a crash.
A hum, then a glow — and then the shell burst into
a shower of warm little lights, like tiny stars learning to fly.
And in the middle of all that shine sat a small green boy, blinking.
Calm.
Quiet.
Like he had known, all along, that this was his moment.
then opening wide; the gold light he is made of pouring out; indigo night behind.
Somewhere in you, there is a light. Even the dark knows your name.
The Valley of Quiet Eggs had a rule: eggs hatch birds.
Always birds.
Nobody had ever seen a boy come out of an egg.
"Who is he?" they whispered.
"What is he?"
But Kole the Keeper already knew.
He had heard the hum for seven years
from the hum-nest on the hill.
So he smiled his slow smile and said:
"That is Mo.
He was not waiting to hatch.
He was waiting to SHINE."
from windows, heads tilted; Kole front, lantern-staff tall, calm and sure;
Mo, Mo, small and slow. Wait with the egg. And watch it glow.
But growing is not the same as knowing.
Mo tried to talk to birds (they chirped and flew).
Mo tried to sit like stones
(he could not).
Nothing worked like it should, and the light inside him
started to ache.
He asked Kole: "What if I crack again?"
(fail), shoulders drooping; behind his chest a tiny gold glow, dimmer now;
Kole listening, lantern-staff light steadying Mo's shadow.
Mo, Mo, small and slow. Wait with the egg. And watch it glow.
Kole said: "Everyone carries an egg inside.
Most folks keep it shut their
whole life, because cracks look scary.
But hear me, little light:
The crack was never breaking.
The crack was BECOMING."
So Mo stopped squeezing his fear, and started listening instead.
And deep inside, something beautiful answered his hum.
Ukweeee.
the glow now BRIGHT again; Mo's face lit from within, eyes wide with wonder;
the dark around soft, warm, owl + moth + fireflies present.
Mo, Mo, small and slow. Wait with the egg. And watch it glow.
That night, Mo dreamed of the day he would shine again — a bigger shine,
that helps the whole valley find things they lost in the dark.
When the valley was quiet, Mo whispered the secret to himself, one time:
"The crack was not breaking.
It was becoming."
And far away on the hill, one small egg hummed back.
